title: Introduce RAG Journey Kit: Node + WASM bridge playground, authoring walkthrough, and telemetry notes
author: Aisha Kumar
body:
Context: a lot of teams want a minimal reproducible RAG + agent dev loop that runs locally and can exercise browser-embedded tool-calls and a small WASM bridge for edge-ish environments. This PR adds a compact "RAG Journey Kit" that includes a Node runner, a tiny browser sandbox, a WASM bridge module (Rust->WASM shim, prebuilt for the sandbox), authoring walkthrough docs, and telemetry presets for offline debugging.

What this delivers: 1) examples/rag-journey-kit: complete quickstart with stepwise authoring guide and testing checklist; 2) packages/wasm-bridge: minimal Rust shim and JS loader demonstrating KV-cache-aware token streaming and a small tool-binding contract; 3) examples/browser-sandbox: a static dev playground that loads a pinned model variant via the Redwood hosted API shim (dev token placeholder) and shows structured output + tool-call roundtrip; 4) docs/site/quickstarts/rag-journey-kit.md: docsite page with screenshots, API snippets, and recommended telemetry probes.

Checklist: [x] Node quickstart and scripts (npm start / npm run smoke) [x] WASM bridge build + prebuilt artifact for sandbox [x] Authoring walkthrough with step checkpoints and prompt fixtures [x] Telemetry presets (dev-level sampling, SDTM events) [x] E2E smoke CI (headless browser) [ ] Optional: CouchDB backend indexer example (follow-up PR)

Motivation: provide a low-friction path for engineers to iterate on RAG prompt variants, exercise tool-calling in-browser, and observe token-level telemetry without spinning up heavy infra. The WASM bridge demonstrates how small edge adapters can implement tool contracts and forward structured tool calls back to an agent runtime.

Testing summary: ran local smoke runner (node) and headless sandbox CI. Verified structured output linter catches contract violations and fallback to textual tool-calls works. Measured cold-start time in the sandbox: ~420ms to first token on dev hardware.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the authoring walkthrough language (docs/site changes) and the tool contract shape in packages/wasm-bridge/bridge.rs. The WASM code is intentionally small; we intentionally avoided adding a full KV store implementation and instead provide a clear adapter surface for integration.

Related: references ENG-8642 (authoring kit), RFC-79 (wasm bridge spec), and local-eval templates used in telemetry playbooks.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice minimal surface. A few nits on wording in the quickstart; can we clarify the distinction between 'tool-call' and 'external tool' in the browser sandbox README?
Aisha Kumar (author): Thanks Liam! Clarified the wording and added a short diagram to the docsite page to show the flow.
Marina Soto: wasm-bridge/lib.rs looks good but can you add a comment about memory growth assumptions? Also prefer exposing a JSON schema for the tool contract rather than ad-hoc objects.
Aisha Kumar (author): Added the schema file under examples/rag-journey-kit/schemas/tool_contract.json and left the memory comment in lib.rs. Kept the bridge intentionally tolerant for demo purposes.
Diego Alvarez: CI flaked on headless job once; rerun fixed it. Add retry in workflow to reduce flakiness.
Aisha Kumar (author): Added retry step in .github/workflows/headless-sandbox-smoke.yml and increased Puppeteer timeout.
